这是一个 Microsoft 提供的 Windows 通用应用平台 (UWP) 示例项目，演示如何使用 C++/CX 开发 Wi-Fi Direct 功能的应用程序。Wi-Fi Direct 是一种允许设备之间直接进行 Wi-Fi 点对点连接的技术，无需通过传统无线接入点（路由器）。

```
├── Scenario2_Connector.xaml*     # 连接者场景实现

└── WiFiDirect.vcxproj            # Visual Studio 项目文件
```

- **功能**：发布 Wi-Fi Direct 广告，等待其他设备连接

  - 配置可发现性级别（Normal/Intensive/None）

  - 监听并接受传入连接请求

@echo off
REM ===========================================================
REM  Wi-Fi Direct CLI Tool - Build Script (MSVC cl.exe)
REM ===========================================================
REM
REM  Prerequisites:
REM    1. Visual Studio 2019/2022 with C++ workload installed
REM    2. Windows SDK 10.0.17763.0 or later (includes C++/WinRT headers)
REM    3. Run from "Developer Command Prompt for VS" or
REM       "x64 Native Tools Command Prompt for VS"
REM
REM  Usage:
REM    build.bat
REM ===========================================================

setlocal enabledelayedexpansion

echo === Wi-Fi Direct CLI Tool Build Script ===
echo.

REM Check if cl.exe is available
where cl.exe >nul 2>&1
if %errorlevel% neq 0 (
    echo ERROR: cl.exe not found.
    echo Please run this script from "Developer Command Prompt for VS 2019/2022"
    echo or "x64 Native Tools Command Prompt for VS 2019/2022".
    echo.
    echo To open it:
    echo   Start Menu ^> Visual Studio 2022 ^> x64 Native Tools Command Prompt
    exit /b 1
)

REM Detect Windows SDK path
set SDK_VERSION=
for /f "tokens=*" %%i in ('dir /b /ad "C:\Program Files (x86)\Windows Kits\10\Include\" 2^>nul ^| findstr "10\." ^| sort /r') do (
    if not defined SDK_VERSION set SDK_VERSION=%%i
)

if not defined SDK_VERSION (
    echo ERROR: Windows SDK not found.
    echo Please install Windows 10 SDK via Visual Studio Installer.
    exit /b 1
)

echo Detected Windows SDK version: %SDK_VERSION%

set SDK_ROOT=C:\Program Files (x86)\Windows Kits\10
set SDK_INC=%SDK_ROOT%\Include\%SDK_VERSION%
set SDK_LIB=%SDK_ROOT%\Lib\%SDK_VERSION%

REM Check for C++/WinRT headers
if not exist "%SDK_INC%\cppwinrt\winrt\Windows.Foundation.h" (
    echo ERROR: C++/WinRT headers not found in SDK.
    echo Please ensure Windows SDK %SDK_VERSION% includes C++/WinRT support.
    echo You can also install cppwinrt NuGet package manually.
    exit /b 1
)

echo C++/WinRT headers found.
echo.

REM Set compiler flags
set CFLAGS=/nologo /EHsc /std:c++17 /W3 /O2
set INCLUDES=/I"%SDK_INC%\cppwinrt" /I"%SDK_INC%\um" /I"%SDK_INC%\ucrt" /I"%SDK_INC%\shared" /I"%SDK_INC%\winrt" /I"."
set LIBS=windowsapp.lib
set LIBPATH=/LIBPATH:"%SDK_LIB%\um\x64" /LIBPATH:"%SDK_LIB%\ucrt\x64"

set OUTPUT=WiFiDirectCLI.exe
set SOURCE=main.cpp

echo Compiling %SOURCE%...
echo.

cl.exe %CFLAGS% %INCLUDES% %SOURCE% /Fe:%OUTPUT% /link %LIBS% %LIBPATH%

if %errorlevel% neq 0 (
    echo.
    echo Build FAILED.
    exit /b 1
)

echo.
echo Build SUCCEEDED: %OUTPUT%
echo.
echo Usage:
echo   %OUTPUT% advertise   - Run as Wi-Fi Direct advertiser
echo   %OUTPUT% connect     - Run as Wi-Fi Direct connector
echo   %OUTPUT% help        - Show help
echo.

endlocal

# Wi-Fi Direct CLI Tool - Build Guide

## Overview

This is a command-line version of the Windows UWP Wi-Fi Direct sample.
It provides the same core functionality (advertising and connecting Wi-Fi Direct devices)
without requiring a graphical user interface or Visual Studio project system.

The code has been converted from C++/CX (UWP) to **C++/WinRT** (standard C++17),
which allows building with the MSVC `cl.exe` compiler from the command line.

## Prerequisites

1. **Windows 10/11** (Build 17763 or later recommended)
2. **Visual Studio 2019 or 2022** with the following components:
   - "Desktop development with C++" workload
   - Windows 10/11 SDK (10.0.17763.0 or later)
   - C++/WinRT support (included in modern SDKs)
3. **No Visual Studio IDE required** - only the build tools are needed.
   You can install "Build Tools for Visual Studio" as a lightweight alternative.

## Build Instructions

### Step 1: Open a Developer Command Prompt

You need a command prompt with the MSVC toolchain configured.

**Option A**: From Start Menu:
```
Start Menu > Visual Studio 2022 > x64 Native Tools Command Prompt for VS 2022
```

**Option B**: Manually initialize:
```cmd
"C:\Program Files\Microsoft Visual Studio\2022\Community\VC\Auxiliary\Build\vcvars64.bat"
```

### Step 2: Navigate to the transform directory

```cmd
cd <path-to-project>\transform
```

### Step 3: Run the build script

```cmd
build.bat
```

This will compile `main.cpp` and produce `WiFiDirectCLI.exe`.

### Manual Build (without build script)

If you prefer to compile manually:

```cmd
cl.exe /nologo /EHsc /std:c++17 /W3 /O2 ^
    /I"C:\Program Files (x86)\Windows Kits\10\Include\<SDK_VERSION>\cppwinrt" ^
    /I"C:\Program Files (x86)\Windows Kits\10\Include\<SDK_VERSION>\um" ^
    /I"C:\Program Files (x86)\Windows Kits\10\Include\<SDK_VERSION>\ucrt" ^
    /I"C:\Program Files (x86)\Windows Kits\10\Include\<SDK_VERSION>\shared" ^
    /I"C:\Program Files (x86)\Windows Kits\10\Include\<SDK_VERSION>\winrt" ^
    main.cpp ^
    /Fe:WiFiDirectCLI.exe ^
    /link windowsapp.lib ^
    /LIBPATH:"C:\Program Files (x86)\Windows Kits\10\Lib\<SDK_VERSION>\um\x64" ^
    /LIBPATH:"C:\Program Files (x86)\Windows Kits\10\Lib\<SDK_VERSION>\ucrt\x64"
```

Replace `<SDK_VERSION>` with your installed SDK version (e.g., `10.0.19041.0`).

## Note on g++ Compatibility

**g++ (MinGW/MSYS2) is NOT supported** for this project because:
- The code uses Windows Runtime (WinRT) APIs, which require the `windowsapp.lib` import library
- C++/WinRT headers are MSVC-specific and rely on MSVC extensions
- The `/await` and WinRT projection features are MSVC-only

The MSVC `cl.exe` compiler is the only supported compiler for WinRT-based applications.
The build script and instructions are designed to work from the command line without
needing to open the Visual Studio IDE.

# Wi-Fi Direct CLI Tool - Usage Guide

## Overview

WiFiDirectCLI is a command-line tool for Windows that allows you to:
- **Advertise** a Wi-Fi Direct service and accept incoming connections
- **Connect** to nearby Wi-Fi Direct devices

This tool was converted from the Microsoft UWP Wi-Fi Direct sample,
removing the graphical interface and replacing it with an interactive CLI.

## Quick Start

```cmd
WiFiDirectCLI.exe advertise    # Run as advertiser (server)
WiFiDirectCLI.exe connect      # Run as connector (client)
WiFiDirectCLI.exe help         # Show help
```

## Advertiser Mode

The advertiser publishes a Wi-Fi Direct advertisement so other devices can discover and connect to it.

### Startup Options

When you start advertiser mode, you will be prompted for:

| Option | Description | Default |
|--------|-------------|---------|
| Listen State | Discoverability level (Normal/Intensive/None) | Normal |
| Autonomous GO | Enable autonomous group owner mode | No |
| Connection Listener | Enable listener for incoming connections | Yes |
| GO Intent | Group owner intent value (0-15) | 14 |

### Interactive Commands

Once the advertisement is running:

| Command | Description |
|---------|-------------|
| `list` | Show all connected devices |
| `send <index> <message>` | Send a text message to device at the given index |
| `close <index>` | Close connection to device at the given index |
| `stop` | Stop advertising and exit |

### Example Session

```
WiFiDirectCLI.exe advertise

=== Wi-Fi Direct Advertiser Mode ===
Options:
  [1] Listen State: Normal (default)
  [2] Listen State: Intensive
  [3] Listen State: None
Select listen state [1-3]: 1
Enable Autonomous Group Owner mode? [y/N]: n
Enable connection listener? [Y/n]: y
Group Owner Intent [0-15, default 14]: 14
[Advertiser] Advertisement started, waiting for connections...

> list
No connected devices.
[Advertiser] Connection request received from: DESKTOP-ABC123
Accept connection? [Y/n]: y
[Advertiser] Connecting to DESKTOP-ABC123...
[Advertiser] L2 connected, listening on 192.168.49.1:50001
[Advertiser] Client connected on L4 layer

> list
  [0] Session_12345

> send 0 Hello from advertiser!
[Socket] Sent message: Hello from advertiser!

> close 0
Closed: Session_12345

> stop
[Advertiser] Stopped.
```

## Connector Mode

The connector discovers nearby Wi-Fi Direct devices and connects to them.

### Startup Options

| Option | Description | Default |
|--------|-------------|---------|
| Selector Type | Device Interface or Association Endpoint | Device Interface |
| GO Intent | Group owner intent value (0-15) | 14 |

### Interactive Commands

| Command | Description |
|---------|-------------|
| `devices` | List all discovered Wi-Fi Direct devices |
| `connect <index>` | Connect to a discovered device at the given index |
| `list` | Show all connected (established) sessions |
| `send <index> <message>` | Send a text message to connected device |
| `close <index>` | Close connection to device at the given index |
| `stop` | Stop watcher and exit |

### Example Session

```
WiFiDirectCLI.exe connect

=== Wi-Fi Direct Connector Mode ===
Device selector type:
  [1] Device Interface (default)
  [2] Association Endpoint
Select [1-2]: 1
Group Owner Intent [0-15, default 14]: 14
[Connector] Watching for Wi-Fi Direct devices...

[Watcher] Device found: MyLaptop-Direct (Total: 1)
[Watcher] Device found: Phone-WiFiDirect (Total: 2)
[Watcher] Enumeration completed.

> devices
  [0] MyLaptop-Direct (WiFiDirect#xxx)
  [1] Phone-WiFiDirect (WiFiDirect#yyy)

> connect 0
[Connector] Connecting to MyLaptop-Direct...
[Connector] L2 connected, connecting to 192.168.49.1:50001
[Connector] Waiting for server socket...
[Connector] Connected on L4 layer, session: Session_54321

> send 0 Hello from connector!
[Socket] Sent message: Hello from connector!

> stop
[Connector] Stopped.
```

## Typical Workflow

To test Wi-Fi Direct communication between two Windows machines:

1. **Machine A** (Advertiser):
   ```cmd
   WiFiDirectCLI.exe advertise
   ```

2. **Machine B** (Connector):
   ```cmd
   WiFiDirectCLI.exe connect
   ```

3. On Machine B, use `devices` to find Machine A, then `connect <index>`
4. On Machine A, accept the connection when prompted
5. Use `send` on either machine to exchange messages

## Requirements

- Windows 10 (Build 17763+) or Windows 11
- Wi-Fi adapter that supports Wi-Fi Direct
- Administrator privileges may be required for Wi-Fi Direct operations

## Troubleshooting

| Issue | Solution |
|-------|----------|
| "No devices discovered" | Ensure Wi-Fi is enabled and the other device is advertising |
| "Connection error" | Check firewall settings, ensure port 50001 is not blocked |
| "FromIdAsync failed" | Try running as Administrator |
| "Status changed: error" | Wi-Fi adapter may not support Wi-Fi Direct |

## Architecture

```
Original UWP App          -->     CLI Tool
----------------------------------------------
XAML UI + Event Handlers   -->     stdin/stdout + Interactive Commands
C++/CX                    -->     C++/WinRT (Standard C++17)
Visual Studio Build        -->     cl.exe Command-Line Build
MainPage / Pages           -->     main() + RunAdvertiser() / RunConnector()
MessageDialog              -->     Console prompts
ListView (device list)     -->     std::vector + index-based selection
```

# Wi-Fi Direct CLI Tool

## Overview

This is a command-line Wi-Fi Direct tool converted from the Microsoft UWP WiFiDirect C++/CX sample. It provides the same Wi-Fi Direct functionality (advertising, discovering, connecting, messaging) without requiring a graphical user interface or Visual Studio build system.

**Key Changes from Original UWP Sample:**
- Replaced C++/CX (`ref class`, `^` pointers, `Platform::`) with standard C++/WinRT (C++17)
- Removed all XAML UI dependencies, using console I/O instead
- Removed UWP app model dependency (AppxManifest, App.xaml, etc.)
- Builds as a standard Win32 console application using `cl.exe` from the command line
- No Visual Studio project/solution files needed

## Project Structure

```
transform/
├── main.cpp              # Entry point with main menu
├── pch.h                 # Precompiled header (C++/WinRT & std includes)
├── SocketReaderWriter.h  # Socket helper class, constants, data models
├── Advertiser.h          # Advertiser mode (publish & accept connections)
├── Connector.h           # Connector mode (discover & connect to devices)
├── build.bat             # Build script for cl.exe (MSVC)
├── BUILD.md              # Build instructions (this file)
└── USAGE.md              # Usage instructions
```

## Prerequisites

1. **Windows 10** (version 1809 / Build 17763 or later)
2. **Windows 10 SDK** (10.0.17763.0 or later) — includes C++/WinRT headers
3. **Visual Studio Build Tools** or **Visual Studio** with "Desktop development with C++" workload installed
   - Only the `cl.exe` compiler and Windows SDK are needed; the Visual Studio IDE is NOT required
4. A Wi-Fi adapter that supports Wi-Fi Direct

## Build Instructions

### Method 1: Using the build script (Recommended)

1. Open **"x64 Native Tools Command Prompt for VS 2019/2022"** (or "Developer Command Prompt for VS")
   - You can find this in the Start Menu under Visual Studio folder
   - This sets up all the necessary environment variables for `cl.exe`

2. Navigate to the `transform` directory:
   ```cmd
   cd path\to\WiFiDirect\cpp\transform
   ```

3. Run the build script:
   ```cmd
   build.bat
   ```

4. If successful, you'll find `WiFiDirectCLI.exe` in the current directory.

### Method 2: Manual compilation

Open "x64 Native Tools Command Prompt for VS" and run:

```cmd
cl.exe /nologo /EHsc /std:c++17 /W3 /O2 /DWIN32_LEAN_AND_MEAN /DWINRT_LEAN_AND_MEAN /I"%WindowsSdkDir%Include\%WindowsSDKVersion%\cppwinrt" main.cpp /Fe:WiFiDirectCLI.exe /link /SUBSYSTEM:CONSOLE windowsapp.lib
```

### Compiler Flags Explained

| Flag | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `/EHsc` | Enable C++ exception handling |
| `/std:c++17` | C++17 standard (required for C++/WinRT) |
| `/W3` | Warning level 3 |
| `/O2` | Optimize for speed |
| `/DWIN32_LEAN_AND_MEAN` | Exclude rarely-used Windows headers |
| `/DWINRT_LEAN_AND_MEAN` | Minimize WinRT headers |
| `windowsapp.lib` | Link against Windows Runtime umbrella library |
| `/SUBSYSTEM:CONSOLE` | Build as console application |

## Troubleshooting

### "cl.exe not found"
Make sure you're running from a Developer Command Prompt or x64 Native Tools Command Prompt. These prompts set up the PATH and environment variables needed for `cl.exe`.

### "Cannot open include file: winrt/Windows.Foundation.h"
Your Windows 10 SDK might be too old. Update to SDK version 10.0.17763.0 or later, which includes C++/WinRT headers.

### "unresolved external symbol"
Make sure `windowsapp.lib` is being linked. This umbrella library contains all WinRT API imports.

### Runtime errors about capabilities
Wi-Fi Direct requires specific system capabilities. When running as a desktop (non-UWP) app, ensure:
- Your Wi-Fi adapter supports Wi-Fi Direct
- Wi-Fi is enabled
- Run as Administrator if needed

## Note on g++ (MinGW/GCC)

C++/WinRT relies on Windows-specific headers and the `windowsapp.lib` import library, which are part of the Windows SDK. **MinGW/GCC (`g++`) does not support C++/WinRT** because it lacks the necessary Windows SDK integration. The `cl.exe` (MSVC) compiler is the only supported compiler for this project.

If cross-platform compilation is needed, consider wrapping the Wi-Fi Direct functionality behind an abstraction layer and providing platform-specific implementations.

# Wi-Fi Direct CLI Tool - Usage Guide

## Quick Start

```cmd
WiFiDirectCLI.exe
```

The tool presents a main menu with two modes:

```
========================================
       Wi-Fi Direct CLI Tool
========================================
  1. Advertiser Mode (publish & accept connections)
  2. Connector Mode  (discover & connect to devices)
  0. Exit
========================================
Select mode:
```

## Mode 1: Advertiser

Use this mode to **publish** a Wi-Fi Direct advertisement and **accept** incoming connections from other devices.

### Workflow

1. Select **1** from the main menu
2. Select **1** (Start Advertisement) from the Advertiser menu
3. Configure the following options when prompted:
   - **Enable listener**: `y` to accept incoming connections
   - **Prefer Group Owner mode**: `y` to act as group owner
   - **Listen State Discoverability**: `0` (Normal), `1` (Intensive), or `2` (None)
   - **Group Owner Intent**: `0`-`15` (higher = more likely to be group owner)
4. The advertisement is now active. Other devices can discover and connect to this device.
5. When a connection request arrives, it is **auto-accepted** (no dialog box in CLI mode)
6. After connection, use option **4** to send messages and **5** to list connected devices

### Advertiser Menu Options

| Option | Action |
|--------|--------|
| 1 | Start Advertisement — begin broadcasting |
| 2 | Stop Advertisement — stop broadcasting |
| 3 | Add Information Element — attach custom data to the advertisement |
| 4 | Send Message — send text to a connected device |
| 5 | List Connected Devices — show all current connections |
| 6 | Close Connection — disconnect from a specific device |
| 0 | Back to main menu |

### Adding Information Elements (IE)

Information Elements allow you to attach custom metadata to your Wi-Fi Direct advertisement:

1. Select **3** from the Advertiser menu
2. Enter any text string (this is encoded as a custom IE with OUI `AA:BB:CC`)
3. The IE will be visible to Connector devices when they scan

## Mode 2: Connector

Use this mode to **discover** nearby Wi-Fi Direct devices and **connect** to them.

### Workflow

1. Select **2** from the main menu
2. Select **1** (Start Device Watcher) from the Connector menu
3. Choose device selector type:
   - `0` = DeviceInterface (faster, finds currently active devices)
   - `1` = AssociationEndpoint (slower, finds more devices)
4. Wait for devices to be discovered (you'll see log messages)
5. Select **3** to list discovered devices
6. Select **5** to connect to a specific device (enter its index and GO Intent)
7. After connection, use option **6** to send messages

### Connector Menu Options

| Option | Action |
|--------|--------|
| 1 | Start Device Watcher — begin scanning for devices |
| 2 | Stop Device Watcher — stop scanning |
| 3 | List Discovered Devices — show found devices with IDs |
| 4 | Show Information Elements — view IEs of a discovered device |
| 5 | Connect to Device — establish a Wi-Fi Direct connection |
| 6 | Send Message — send text to a connected device |
| 7 | List Connected Devices — show active connections |
| 8 | Close Connection — disconnect from a device |
| 0 | Back to main menu |

## Typical Two-Device Scenario

### Device A (Advertiser):
```
Select mode: 1
Select: 1
Enable listener for incoming connections? (y/n): y
Prefer Group Owner mode? (y/n): y
Listen State Discoverability (0=Normal, 1=Intensive, 2=None): 0
Group Owner Intent (0-15): 14
```

### Device B (Connector):
```
Select mode: 2
Select: 1
Device selector type (0=DeviceInterface, 1=AssociationEndpoint): 1
(wait for discovery)
Select: 3
(list shows Device A)
Select: 5
Select device index to connect: 0
Group Owner Intent (0-15): 1
(connection established)
Select: 6
Select device index: 0
Enter message: Hello from Device B!
```

## Communication Protocol

Messages are sent using a simple length-prefixed protocol:
- 4 bytes (uint32, little-endian): message length in bytes
- N bytes: UTF-8 encoded message string

This is the same protocol used in the original UWP sample.

## Server Port

The default server port for L4 (TCP socket) connections is **50001**. This is hardcoded in `SocketReaderWriter.h` as `strServerPort`.

## Error Handling

- Errors are printed to stderr with `[ERROR]` prefix
- Informational messages are printed to stdout with `[INFO]` prefix
- Most exceptions are caught and displayed with descriptive messages
- If a connection fails, you can retry without restarting the application

## Limitations

- This tool must be run on **Windows 10** (Build 17763+) with a Wi-Fi Direct capable adapter
- The Wi-Fi Direct APIs are Windows-specific and cannot run on Linux/macOS
- When running as a desktop app (not UWP), some Wi-Fi Direct features may require running as Administrator
- Only one advertisement can be active at a time per adapter

REM ===========================================================
REM  Wi-Fi Direct CLI Tool - Build Script (MSVC cl.exe)
REM ===========================================================
REM
REM  Prerequisites:
REM    1. Visual Studio 2019/2022 with "Desktop development with C++"
REM    2. Windows SDK 10.0.17763.0 or later (with C++/WinRT headers)
REM    3. Run from "x64 Native Tools Command Prompt for VS"
REM
REM  Usage:
REM    build.bat
REM ===========================================================

setlocal enabledelayedexpansion

echo === Wi-Fi Direct CLI Tool Build Script ===
echo.

REM Check if cl.exe is available
where cl.exe >nul 2>&1
if %errorlevel% neq 0 (
    echo ERROR: cl.exe not found.
    echo Please run this script from "Developer Command Prompt for VS 2019/2022"
    echo or "x64 Native Tools Command Prompt for VS 2019/2022".
    echo.
    echo To open it:
    echo   Start Menu ^> Visual Studio 2022 ^> x64 Native Tools Command Prompt
    exit /b 1
)

REM Detect Windows SDK path
set SDK_VERSION=
for /f "tokens=*" %%i in ('dir /b /ad "C:\Program Files (x86)\Windows Kits\10\Include\" 2^>nul ^| findstr "10\." ^| sort /r') do (
    if not defined SDK_VERSION set SDK_VERSION=%%i
)

if not defined SDK_VERSION (
    echo ERROR: Windows SDK not found.
    echo Please install Windows 10/11 SDK via Visual Studio Installer.
    exit /b 1
)

echo Detected Windows SDK version: %SDK_VERSION%

set SDK_ROOT=C:\Program Files (x86)\Windows Kits\10
set SDK_INC=%SDK_ROOT%\Include\%SDK_VERSION%
set SDK_LIB=%SDK_ROOT%\Lib\%SDK_VERSION%

REM Check for C++/WinRT headers
if not exist "%SDK_INC%\cppwinrt\winrt\Windows.Foundation.h" (
    echo ERROR: C++/WinRT headers not found in SDK.
    echo Please ensure Windows SDK %SDK_VERSION% includes C++/WinRT support.
    echo.
    echo You can install C++/WinRT via:
    echo   1. Visual Studio Installer ^> Modify ^> Individual components ^> C++/WinRT
    echo   2. Or: nuget install Microsoft.Windows.CppWinRT
    exit /b 1
)

echo C++/WinRT headers found.
echo.

REM Compiler and linker flags
set CFLAGS=/nologo /EHsc /std:c++17 /W3 /O2 /DWIN32_LEAN_AND_MEAN /D_UNICODE /DUNICODE
set INCLUDES=/I"%SDK_INC%\cppwinrt" /I"%SDK_INC%\um" /I"%SDK_INC%\ucrt" /I"%SDK_INC%\shared" /I"%SDK_INC%\winrt" /I"."
set LIBS=windowsapp.lib ole32.lib
set LIBPATH=/LIBPATH:"%SDK_LIB%\um\x64" /LIBPATH:"%SDK_LIB%\ucrt\x64"

set OUTPUT=WiFiDirectCLI.exe
set SOURCE=main.cpp

echo Compiling %SOURCE%...
echo.

cl.exe %CFLAGS% %INCLUDES% %SOURCE% /Fe:%OUTPUT% /link %LIBS% %LIBPATH%

if %errorlevel% neq 0 (
    echo.
    echo Build FAILED.
    exit /b 1
)

echo.
echo ========================================
echo Build SUCCEEDED: %OUTPUT%
echo ========================================
echo.
echo Usage:
echo   %OUTPUT% advertise   - Run as Wi-Fi Direct advertiser
echo   %OUTPUT% connect     - Run as Wi-Fi Direct connector
echo   %OUTPUT% help        - Show help
echo.

endlocal

# Wi-Fi Direct CLI Tool

## Overview

This is a command-line Wi-Fi Direct tool converted from the Microsoft UWP WiFiDirect C++/CX sample. It provides the same Wi-Fi Direct functionality (advertising, discovering, connecting, messaging) without requiring a graphical user interface or Visual Studio build system.

**Key Changes from Original UWP Sample:**
- Replaced C++/CX (`ref class`, `^` pointers, `Platform::`) with standard C++/WinRT (C++17)
- Removed all XAML UI dependencies, using console I/O instead
- Removed UWP app model dependency (AppxManifest, App.xaml, etc.)
- Builds as a standard Win32 console application using `cl.exe` from the command line
- No Visual Studio project/solution files needed

## Project Structure

```
transform/
├── main.cpp              # Entry point, Advertiser & Connector modes (single file)
├── pch.h                 # Precompiled header (C++/WinRT & std includes)
├── SocketReaderWriter.h  # Socket helper class, constants, data models, logging
├── build.bat             # Build script for cl.exe (MSVC)
├── BUILD.md              # Build instructions (this file)
└── USAGE.md              # Usage instructions
```

## Prerequisites

1. **Windows 10** (version 1809 / Build 17763 or later)
2. **Windows 10 SDK** (10.0.17763.0 or later) — includes C++/WinRT headers
3. **Visual Studio Build Tools** or **Visual Studio** with "Desktop development with C++" workload installed
   - Only the `cl.exe` compiler and Windows SDK are needed; the Visual Studio IDE is NOT required
4. A Wi-Fi adapter that supports Wi-Fi Direct

## Build Instructions

### Method 1: Using the build script (Recommended)

1. Open **"x64 Native Tools Command Prompt for VS 2019/2022"** (or "Developer Command Prompt for VS")
   - You can find this in the Start Menu under Visual Studio folder
   - This sets up all the necessary environment variables for `cl.exe`

2. Navigate to the `transform` directory:
   ```cmd
   cd path\to\WiFiDirect\cpp\transform
   ```

3. Run the build script:
   ```cmd
   build.bat
   ```

4. If successful, you'll find `WiFiDirectCLI.exe` in the current directory.

### Method 2: Manual compilation

Open "x64 Native Tools Command Prompt for VS" and run:

```cmd
cl.exe /nologo /EHsc /std:c++17 /W3 /O2 /DWIN32_LEAN_AND_MEAN /DWINRT_LEAN_AND_MEAN /I"%WindowsSdkDir%Include\%WindowsSDKVersion%\cppwinrt" main.cpp /Fe:WiFiDirectCLI.exe /link /SUBSYSTEM:CONSOLE windowsapp.lib
```

### Compiler Flags Explained

| Flag | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `/EHsc` | Enable C++ exception handling |
| `/std:c++17` | C++17 standard (required for C++/WinRT) |
| `/W3` | Warning level 3 |
| `/O2` | Optimize for speed |
| `/DWIN32_LEAN_AND_MEAN` | Exclude rarely-used Windows headers |
| `/DWINRT_LEAN_AND_MEAN` | Minimize WinRT headers |
| `windowsapp.lib` | Link against Windows Runtime umbrella library |
| `/SUBSYSTEM:CONSOLE` | Build as console application |

## Troubleshooting

### "cl.exe not found"
Make sure you're running from a Developer Command Prompt or x64 Native Tools Command Prompt. These prompts set up the PATH and environment variables needed for `cl.exe`.

### "Cannot open include file: winrt/Windows.Foundation.h"
Your Windows 10 SDK might be too old. Update to SDK version 10.0.17763.0 or later, which includes C++/WinRT headers.

### "unresolved external symbol"
Make sure `windowsapp.lib` is being linked. This umbrella library contains all WinRT API imports.

### Runtime errors about capabilities
Wi-Fi Direct requires specific system capabilities. When running as a desktop (non-UWP) app, ensure:
- Your Wi-Fi adapter supports Wi-Fi Direct
- Wi-Fi is enabled
- Run as Administrator if needed

## Note on g++ (MinGW/GCC)

C++/WinRT relies on Windows-specific headers and the `windowsapp.lib` import library, which are part of the Windows SDK. **MinGW/GCC (`g++`) does not support C++/WinRT** because it lacks the necessary Windows SDK integration. The `cl.exe` (MSVC) compiler is the only supported compiler for this project.

If cross-platform compilation is needed, consider wrapping the Wi-Fi Direct functionality behind an abstraction layer and providing platform-specific implementations.

# Wi-Fi Direct CLI Tool - Build Guide

## Overview

This is a command-line version of the Windows UWP Wi-Fi Direct sample.
It provides the same core functionality (advertising and connecting Wi-Fi Direct devices)
without requiring a graphical user interface or the Visual Studio IDE project system.

The code has been converted from **C++/CX (UWP)** to **C++/WinRT (standard C++17)**,
which allows building with the MSVC `cl.exe` compiler directly from the command line.

## Project Structure

```
transform/
├── main.cpp              # Main CLI entry point (advertiser + connector modes)
├── pch.h                 # Precompiled header (WinRT + standard includes)
├── SocketReaderWriter.h  # Socket R/W helper, data structures, constants
├── build.bat             # Automated build script for cl.exe
├── BUILD.md              # This file (build instructions)
└── USAGE.md              # Usage documentation
```

## Prerequisites

1. **Windows 10/11** (Build 17763 or later)
2. **Visual Studio Build Tools** (2019 or 2022) with:
   - "Desktop development with C++" workload
   - Windows 10/11 SDK (10.0.17763.0 or later)
   - C++/WinRT support (included in modern Windows SDKs)

> **Note**: The full Visual Studio IDE is NOT required. You can install just the
> [Build Tools for Visual Studio](https://visualstudio.microsoft.com/downloads/#build-tools-for-visual-studio-2022)
> as a lightweight alternative.

## Build Instructions

### Step 1: Open a Developer Command Prompt

You need a command prompt with the MSVC `cl.exe` toolchain configured.

**Option A** - From Start Menu:
```
Start Menu > Visual Studio 2022 > x64 Native Tools Command Prompt for VS 2022
```

**Option B** - Manually initialize the environment:
```cmd
call "C:\Program Files\Microsoft Visual Studio\2022\Community\VC\Auxiliary\Build\vcvars64.bat"
```

### Step 2: Navigate to the transform directory

```cmd
cd path\to\Samples\WiFiDirect\cpp\transform
```

### Step 3: Run the build script

```cmd
build.bat
```

On success, this produces `WiFiDirectCLI.exe` in the current directory.

### Manual Build (without build.bat)

```cmd
cl.exe /nologo /EHsc /std:c++17 /W3 /O2 /DWIN32_LEAN_AND_MEAN /D_UNICODE /DUNICODE ^
    /I"C:\Program Files (x86)\Windows Kits\10\Include\<SDK_VER>\cppwinrt" ^
    /I"C:\Program Files (x86)\Windows Kits\10\Include\<SDK_VER>\um" ^
    /I"C:\Program Files (x86)\Windows Kits\10\Include\<SDK_VER>\ucrt" ^
    /I"C:\Program Files (x86)\Windows Kits\10\Include\<SDK_VER>\shared" ^
    /I"C:\Program Files (x86)\Windows Kits\10\Include\<SDK_VER>\winrt" ^
    /I"." ^
    main.cpp ^
    /Fe:WiFiDirectCLI.exe ^
    /link windowsapp.lib ole32.lib ^
    /LIBPATH:"C:\Program Files (x86)\Windows Kits\10\Lib\<SDK_VER>\um\x64" ^
    /LIBPATH:"C:\Program Files (x86)\Windows Kits\10\Lib\<SDK_VER>\ucrt\x64"
```

Replace `<SDK_VER>` with your installed SDK version (e.g., `10.0.22621.0`).

## Why Not g++?

**g++ (MinGW/MSYS2) is NOT supported** because:
- The code uses Windows Runtime (WinRT) APIs via C++/WinRT projection headers
- C++/WinRT requires `windowsapp.lib` (MSVC import library)
- C++/WinRT headers depend on MSVC-specific features and compiler support

The MSVC `cl.exe` compiler is the **only** supported compiler for WinRT-based applications.
However, no Visual Studio IDE or `.sln`/`.vcxproj` files are needed — everything builds
from a single `cl.exe` command on the command line.

## Troubleshooting

| Issue | Solution |
|-------|----------|
| `cl.exe not found` | Run from "x64 Native Tools Command Prompt" |
| `Windows SDK not found` | Install Windows SDK via Visual Studio Installer |
| `C++/WinRT headers not found` | Update SDK or install `Microsoft.Windows.CppWinRT` NuGet |
| `windowsapp.lib not found` | Ensure SDK lib path is correct for your architecture (x64) |


- `connect` — Start as Wi-Fi Direct connector (client)
- `help` — Show help message

## Mode: Advertiser (`advertise`)

```cmd
WiFiDirectCLI.exe advertise
```

Use this mode to **publish** a Wi-Fi Direct advertisement and **accept** incoming connections from other devices.

### Setup Prompts

When starting, you'll be asked to configure:

```
Listen State (0=Normal, 1=Intensive, 2=None) [0]:
Enable Autonomous Group Owner mode? (y/n) [n]:
Enable connection listener? (y/n) [y]:
Group Owner Intent (0-15) [14]:
```

- **Listen State**: Controls discoverability (Normal is recommended)
- **Autonomous Group Owner**: If `y`, this device will always be the group owner
- **Connection listener**: If `y`, automatically accepts incoming connections
- **Group Owner Intent**: Higher value = more likely to be group owner (0-15)

Press Enter to accept default values shown in `[brackets]`.

### Interactive Commands

After the advertisement starts, you can type commands:

| Command | Description |
|---------|-------------|
| `list` | List all connected devices |
| `send <index> <message>` | Send a text message to a connected device |
| `close <index>` | Close connection to a specific device |
| `addie <text>` | Add a custom Information Element to the advertisement |
| `stop` | Stop advertisement and return |

### Example Session

```
> WiFiDirectCLI.exe advertise
=== Wi-Fi Direct Advertiser Mode ===
Listen State (0=Normal, 1=Intensive, 2=None) [0]:
Enable Autonomous Group Owner mode? (y/n) [n]: y
Enable connection listener? (y/n) [y]:
Group Owner Intent (0-15) [14]:
[INFO]  Advertisement started, waiting for connections...

> list

(after a device connects...)
[INFO]  Connection request received from Device-B
[INFO]  Auto-accepting connection...
[INFO]  Devices connected on L2, listening on IP Address: 192.168.49.1 Port: 50001
[INFO]  Connected with remote side on L4 layer

> list
  [0] Session_12345

> send 0 Hello from advertiser!
[INFO]  Sent message: Hello from advertiser!

> stop
[INFO]  Advertiser stopped.
```

## Mode: Connector (`connect`)

```cmd
WiFiDirectCLI.exe connect
```

Use this mode to **discover** nearby Wi-Fi Direct devices and **connect** to them.

### Setup Prompts

```
Device selector type (0=DeviceInterface, 1=AssociationEndpoint) [0]:
Group Owner Intent (0-15) [14]:
```

- **DeviceInterface** (0): Faster, finds currently active devices
- **AssociationEndpoint** (1): Slower, finds more devices including those not currently active
- **Group Owner Intent**: Lower value = prefer the other side to be group owner

### Interactive Commands

| Command | Description |
|---------|-------------|
| `devices` | List all discovered Wi-Fi Direct devices |
| `connect <index>` | Connect to a discovered device by index |
| `list` | List all active connections |
| `send <index> <message>` | Send a text message to a connected device |
| `close <index>` | Close a specific connection |
| `ie <index>` | Show Information Elements for a discovered device |
| `stop` | Stop device watcher and return |

### Example Session

```
> WiFiDirectCLI.exe connect
=== Wi-Fi Direct Connector Mode ===
Device selector type (0=DeviceInterface, 1=AssociationEndpoint) [0]: 1
Group Owner Intent (0-15) [14]: 1
[INFO]  Watching for Wi-Fi Direct devices...

> devices
  [0] Device-A (WiFiDirect#xx:xx:xx:xx:xx:xx)

> connect 0
[INFO]  Connecting to Device-A...
[INFO]  L2 connected, connecting to 192.168.49.1:50001
[INFO]  Waiting for server socket...
[INFO]  Connected on L4 layer, session: Session_67890
[INFO]  Sent message: Session_67890

> send 0 Hello from connector!
[INFO]  Sent message: Hello from connector!

> list
  [0] Session_67890

> close 0
[INFO]  Session_67890 closed successfully

> stop
[INFO]  Connector stopped.
```

## Typical Two-Device Scenario

### Device A (Advertiser):
```cmd
WiFiDirectCLI.exe advertise
```
Accept defaults or configure as needed. The advertisement starts immediately.

### Device B (Connector):
```cmd
WiFiDirectCLI.exe connect
```
Wait for Device A to appear in `devices` list, then use `connect 0` to connect.

Once connected, both sides can exchange messages using `send`.

## Communication Protocol

Messages use a simple length-prefixed protocol:
- 4 bytes (uint32, little-endian): message length in bytes
- N bytes: UTF-8 encoded message string

This is the same protocol used in the original UWP sample.

## Server Port

The default server port for L4 (TCP socket) connections is **50001**, defined in `SocketReaderWriter.h`.

## Output Format

- `[INFO]` — Informational messages (stdout)
- `[ERROR]` — Error messages (stderr)

## Limitations

- This tool must run on **Windows 10** (Build 17763+) with a Wi-Fi Direct capable adapter
- Wi-Fi Direct APIs are Windows-specific (no Linux/macOS support)
- Running as a desktop app may require Administrator privileges for some features
- Only one advertisement can be active at a time per adapter

已重写 [`build.bat`](command:gongfeng.gongfeng-copilot.chat.open-relative-path?%7B%22%24mid%22%3A1%2C%22fsPath%22%3A%22%2FUsers%2Fjunjiecui%2Fworkspace%2FWindows-universal-samples-main%2FSamples%2FWiFiDirect%2Fcpp%2Ftransform%2Fbuild.bat%22%2C%22path%22%3A%22%2FUsers%2Fjunjiecui%2Fworkspace%2FWindows-universal-samples-main%2FSamples%2FWiFiDirect%2Fcpp%2Ftransform%2Fbuild.bat%22%2C%22scheme%22%3A%22file%22%7D)，主要改动：

2. **自动检测 SDK 路径**：优先使用 VS Developer Prompt 设置的 `%WindowsSdkDir%` 和 `%WindowsSDKVersion%` 环境变量，不再硬编码 [`E:\My_environment\windows_sdk`](command:gongfeng.gongfeng-copilot.chat.open-symbol-in-file?%5B%7B%22%24mid%22%3A1%2C%22fsPath%22%3A%22%2FUsers%2Fjunjiecui%2Fworkspace%2FWindows-universal-samples-main%2FSamples%2FWiFiDirect%2Fcpp%2Ftransform%2Ftmp.log%22%2C%22external%22%3A%22file%3A%2F%2F%2FUsers%2Fjunjiecui%2Fworkspace%2FWindows-universal-samples-main%2FSamples%2FWiFiDirect%2Fcpp%2Ftransform%2Ftmp.log%22%2C%22path%22%3A%22%2FUsers%2Fjunjiecui%2Fworkspace%2FWindows-universal-samples-main%2FSamples%2FWiFiDirect%2Fcpp%2Ftransform%2Ftmp.log%22%2C%22scheme%22%3A%22file%22%7D%2C%22E%3A%5C%5CMy_environment%5C%5Cwindows_sdk%22%2C%5B%7B%22line%22%3A353%2C%22character%22%3A0%7D%2C%7B%22line%22%3A353%2C%22character%22%3A1%7D%5D%5D)

4. **库路径匹配架构**：`/LIBPATH:"%SDK_LIB%\um\%ARCH%"` 和 `/LIBPATH:"%SDK_LIB%\ucrt\%ARCH%"` 确保 lib 目录与编译器架构一致
5. **显式添加 `/SUBSYSTEM:CONSOLE`** 到链接参数
